questions.stem:
The Venn diagram shows the probabilities associated with four events, $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$

[Figure: Venn diagram showing four overlapping circles $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$, with region probabilities $0.24$ (in $A \cap B$, outside $D$), $0.07$ (in $B$ only, between $A$ and $C$), $p$ (in $B \cap C$), $q$ (in $D$), $0.16$ (in $A \cap D'$, outside $B$), $r$ (in $C$ only) and $s$ (outside $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$)]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down any pair of mutually exclusive events from $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $A, C$ or $D, B$ or $D, C$ B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for one correct pair. If more than one pair they must all be correct. Condone in a correct probability statement such as $\mathrm{P}(A\cap C)=0$ or correct use of set notation e.g. $A\cap C=\varnothing$ BUT e.g. "P($A$) and P($C$) are mutually exclusive" alone is B0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $\mathrm{P}(B) = 0.4$
(b) find the value of $p$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $[p = 0.4 - 0.07 - 0.24 =]$ $\underline{0.09}$ B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for $p = 0.09$ (Maybe stated in Venn Diagram [VD]) [ If values in VD and text conflict, take text or a value used in a later part]

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given also that $A$ and $B$ are independent
(c) find the value of $q$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $A$ and $B$ independent implies
$\mathrm{P}(A) \times 0.4 = 0.24$ or $(q + 0.16 + 0.24) \times 0.4 = 0.24$ M1
so $\mathrm{P}(A) = 0.6$ and $q = \underline{0.20}$ A1cso
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a correct equation in one variable for P($A$) or $q$ using independence or for seeing both $\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)=\mathrm{P}(A)\times\mathrm{P}(B)$ and $0.24=0.6\times0.4$. A1cso for $q = 0.20$ or exact equivalent (dep on correct use of independence)
- Beware: Use of $\mathrm{P}(A) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(B) = 0.6$ leading to $q = 0.2$ scores M0A0

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Given further that $\mathrm{P}(B' \mid C) = 0.64$
(d) find
(i) the value of $r$
(ii) the value of $s$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d)(i) $\mathrm{P}(B' \mid C) = 0.64$ gives $\dfrac{r}{r+p} = 0.64$ or $\dfrac{r}{r+"0.09"} = 0.64$ M1
$r = 0.64r + 0.64$ "$p$" so $0.36r = 0.0576$ so $r = \underline{0.16}$ A1
(ii) Using sum of probabilities $= 1$ e.g. "0.6" $+ 0.07 + $ "0.25" $+ s = 1$ M1
so $s = \underline{0.08}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for use of $\mathrm{P}(B'\mid C)=0.64$ leading to a correct equation in $r$ and possibly $p$. Can ft their $p$ provided $0 < p < 1$. 1st A1 for $r = 0.16$ or exact equivalent
- 2nd M1 for use of total probability = 1 to form a linear equation in $s$. Allow $p, q, r$ etc Can follow through their values provided each of $p, q, r$ are in [0, 1). 2nd A1 for $s = 0.08$ or exact equivalent

questions.stem:
A random sample of 15 days is taken from the large data set for Perth in June and July 1987.
The scatter diagram in Figure 1 displays the values of two of the variables for these 15 days.

[Figure 1: scatter diagram, $x$-axis from 0 to 20, $y$-axis unlabelled, showing 15 points with an increasing trend]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Describe the correlation.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Negative B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for stating negative. "Negative skew" is B0 though

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The variable on the $x$-axis is Daily Mean Temperature measured in \textdegree C.
(b) Using your knowledge of the large data set,
(i) suggest which variable is on the $y$-axis,
(ii) state the units that are used in the large data set for this variable.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(i) Rainfall or Pressure B1
(ii) mm or hPa or Pascals or hectopascals or mb or millibars B1ft
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (i) B1 for mentioning "rainfall" (allow "rain" or "precipitation") or "pressure" (if more than 1 answer both must be correct) NB the other quantitative variable for Perth is: Daily Mean Wind Speed and scores B0 [Not allowed "wind speed" since $r = +0.15$ and in winter might expect wind to raise temp]
- (ii) B1ft for giving the correct units. If Daily Mean Wind Speed (kn) or knots "Wind speed" and "knots" would score B0B1 but any other variable scores B0B0
parts.notes: LDS convention: the paired variable and its units come from the large data set's own variable list (spec other_requirements: large data set).

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Stav believes that there is a correlation between Daily Total Sunshine and
Daily Maximum Relative Humidity at Heathrow.

He calculates the product moment correlation coefficient between these two variables
for a random sample of 30 days and obtains $r = -0.377$

(c) Carry out a suitable test to investigate Stav's belief at a 5% level of significance.
State clearly

$\bullet$ your hypotheses
$\bullet$ your critical value
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathrm{H_0}: \rho = 0$ $\mathrm{H_1}: \rho \neq 0$ B1
Critical value: $-0.361(0)$ M1
$r < -0.3610$ so significant result and there is evidence of a correlation
between Daily Total Sunshine and Daily Maximum Relative Humidity A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for both hypotheses correct in terms of $\rho$. M1 for the correct critical value compatible with their H1: allow $\pm$ 0.361(0) If the hypotheses are 1-tail then allow cv of $\pm$ 0.3061 e.g. Alternative hypothesis with $r < \pm 0.377$ implies a one-tail test or H0 and H1 in words saying "H0: there is no correlation, H1: there is correlation" is two-tail. If there are no hypotheses (or they are nonsensical) assume 2-tail so M1 for $\pm$ 0.361(0)
- A1 for a correct conclusion in context based on comparing $-0.377$ with their cv. Condone incorrect inequality e.g. $-0.3610 < -0.377$ as long as they reject H0. Do not accept contradictory statements such as "accept H0 so there is evidence of …" Can say "support for Stav's belief"(o.e.e.g. "claim") or "evidence of a correlation between sunshine and humidity" condone "negative correlation" or comments such as "if humidity is high amount of sunshine will be low"

parts.label: d
parts.text:
On a random day at Heathrow the Daily Maximum Relative Humidity was 97%
(d) Comment on the number of hours of sunshine you would expect on that day,
giving a reason for your answer.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) Humidity is high and there is evidence of correlation and $r < 0$
So expect amount of sunshine to be lower than the average for Heathrow(oe) B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for stating low amount of sunshine (o. e.) and some reference to $r < 0$ or fog. Check for the following 2 features: (i) low sunshine: allow $\leqslant 5$ hrs (LDS mean for 2015 is 5.3, humidity 97% is 4.1, $\geqslant$97% is 3.1) (ii) negative correlation may be described in words e.g. "high humidity gives low sunshine" or fog (LDS says >95% humidity is foggy) so less sunshine

questions.stem:
Each member of a group of 27 people was timed when completing a puzzle.
The time taken, $x$ minutes, for each member of the group was recorded.
These times are summarised in the following box and whisker plot.

[Figure: box and whisker plot of Time ($x$ minutes) from 0 to 70, showing a box with median and quartiles between about 15 and 25, whiskers to about 7 and 40, and two outliers marked with crosses at about 46 and 68]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the range of the times.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[68 - 7 =]$ $\underline{61}$ (only) B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for correctly interpreting the box plot to find the range (more than 1 answer is B0)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the interquartile range of the times.
(1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
For these 27 people $\sum x = 607.5$ and $\sum x^2 = 17623.25$
(c) calculate the mean time taken to complete the puzzle,
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\left[\mu \text{ or } \bar{x} = \dfrac{607.5}{27} =\right] = \underline{22.5}$ B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for 22.5 only (or exact equivalent such as $\frac{45}{2}$). Allow 22 mins and 30 secs.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) calculate the standard deviation of the times taken to complete the puzzle.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{17623.25}{27} - "22.5"^2}$ or $\sqrt{146.4629\ldots}$ M1
$= 12.10218\ldots$ awrt $\underline{12.1}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a correct expression including square root. Allow $\sqrt{146}$ or better. Ft their mean. A1 for awrt 12.1. NB Allow use of $s$ = 12.3327… or awrt 12.3

parts.label: e
parts.text:
Taruni defines an outlier as a value more than 3 standard deviations above the mean.
(e) State how many outliers Taruni would say there are in these data, giving a reason for
your answer.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) $\mu + 3\sigma = "22.5" + 3 \times "12.1\ldots" = $ awrt 59 so only $\underline{\text{one}}$ outlier B1ft
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft for a correct calculation or value based on their $\mu$ and $\sigma$ and compatible conclusion

parts.label: f
parts.text:
Adam and Beth also completed the puzzle in $a$ minutes and $b$ minutes respectively,
where $a > b$.
When their times are included with the data of the other 27 people

$\bullet$ the median time increases
$\bullet$ the mean time does not change

(f) Suggest a possible value for $a$ and a possible value for $b$, explaining how your
values satisfy the above conditions.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(f) Median increases implies that both values must be $> 20$ M1
Mean is the same means that $a + b = 45$ M1
So possible values are: e.g. $b = 21$ and $a = 24$ (o.e.) A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 Correct start to the problem and a correct statement about the values based on median Allow if their final two values are both >20. 2nd M1 for a correct explanation leading to equation $a + b = 45$ (o.e. e.g. equidistant from mean) Allow if their final two values sum to 45
- A1 for a correct pair of values (both > 20 with a sum of 45) and at least some attempt to explain how their values satisfy at least one of the conditions (both > 20 or $a + b = 45$). Ignore $a$ = or $b$ = labels. NB The values for $a$ and $b$ do not need to be integers.

parts.label: g
parts.text:
(g) Without carrying out any further calculations, explain why the standard deviation of
all 29 times will be lower than your answer to part (d).
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(g) Both values will be less than 1 standard deviation from the mean and so the
standard deviation of all 29 values will be smaller B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for a correct explanation. Must mention that both values are less than 1 sd (ft their answer to (d)) from the mean

questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $D$ has the following probability distribution

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline d & 10 & 20 & 30 & 40 & 50\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(D=d) & \dfrac{k}{10} & \dfrac{k}{20} & \dfrac{k}{30} & \dfrac{k}{40} & \dfrac{k}{50}\\ \hline\end{array}$

where $k$ is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the value of $k$ is $\dfrac{600}{137}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\dfrac{k}{10} + \dfrac{k}{20} + \dfrac{k}{30} + \dfrac{k}{40} + \dfrac{k}{50} = 1$ or $\dfrac{1}{600}(60k + 30k + 20k + 15k + 12k) = 1$ M1
So $k = \dfrac{600}{137}$ (*) A1cso
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for clear use of sum of probabilities = 1 (all terms seen). A1 cso (*) M1 scored and no incorrect working seen. Verify (Assume $k = \frac{600}{137}$) to score the final A1 they must have a final comment "$\therefore k = \frac{600}{137}$"

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The random variables $D_1$ and $D_2$ are independent and each have the same distribution as $D$.
(b) Find $\mathrm{P}(D_1 + D_2 = 80)$
Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) (Cases are:) $D_1 = 30, D_2 = 50$ and $D_1 = 50, D_2 = 30$ and $D_1 = 40, D_2 = 40$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(D_1 + D_2 = 80) = \dfrac{k}{50} \times \dfrac{k}{30} \times 2 + \left(\dfrac{k}{40}\right)^2$ M1
$= 0.0375619\ldots$ awrt $\underline{0.0376}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for selecting at least 2 of the relevant cases (may be implied by their correct probs) e.g. allow 30, 50 and 50,30 i.e. $D_1$ and $D_2$ labels not required. 2nd M1 for using the model to obtain a correct expression for two different probabilities. May use letter $k$ or their value for $k$. Allow for $\frac{k}{50}\times\frac{k}{30}+\left(\frac{k}{40}\right)^2$ or $2\times\left(\frac{k}{50}\times\frac{k}{30}+\left(\frac{k}{40}\right)^2\right)$. A1 for awrt 0.0376 (exact fraction is $\frac{705}{18769}$)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A single observation of $D$ is made.

The value obtained, $d$, is the common difference of an arithmetic sequence.

The first 4 terms of this arithmetic sequence are the angles, measured in degrees,
of quadrilateral $Q$

(c) Find the exact probability that the smallest angle of $Q$ is more than $50°$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Angles are: $a$, $a+d$, $a+2d$, $a+3d$ M1
$S_4 = a + (a+d) + (a+2d) + (a+3d) = 360$ M1
$2a + 3d = 180$ (o.e.) A1
Smallest angle is $a > 50$ consider cases:
$d = 10$ so $a = 75$ or $d = 20$ so $a = 60$ [$d = 30$ gives $a = 45$ no good] M1
$\mathrm{P}(D = 10 \text{ or } 20) = \dfrac{3k}{20} = \dfrac{90}{137}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for recognising the 4 angles and finding expressions in terms of $d$ and their $a$. 2nd M1 for using property of quad with these 4 angles (equation can be un-simplified) Allow these two marks for use of a (possible) value of $d$ e.g. $a + a + 10 + a + 20 + a + 30 = 360$ (If at least 3 cases seen allow A1 for e.g. $4a = 300$) or allow M1M1 for a set of 4 angles with sum 360 and possible value of $d$ (3 cases for A1) e.g. (for $d = 20$) 60, 80, 100, 120
- 1st A1 for $2a + 3d = 180$ condition (o.e.) [Must be in the form $pa + qd = N$]. 3rd M1 for examining cases and getting $d = 10$ and $d = 20$ only. 2nd A1 for $\frac{90}{137}$ or exact equivalent. The correct answer and no obviously incorrect working will score 5/5. A final answer of awrt 0.657 (0.65693…) with no obviously incorrect working scores 4/5

questions.question_text:
The discrete random variable $D$ has the following probability distribution

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline d & 10 & 20 & 30 & 40 & 50\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(D=d) & \dfrac{k}{10} & \dfrac{k}{20} & \dfrac{k}{30} & \dfrac{k}{40} & \dfrac{k}{50}\\ \hline\end{array}$

where $k$ is a constant.
(a) Show that the value of $k$ is $\dfrac{600}{137}$
(2)
The random variables $D_1$ and $D_2$ are independent and each have the same distribution as $D$.
(b) Find $\mathrm{P}(D_1 + D_2 = 80)$
Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
(3)
A single observation of $D$ is made.

The value obtained, $d$, is the common difference of an arithmetic sequence.

The first 4 terms of this arithmetic sequence are the angles, measured in degrees,
of quadrilateral $Q$

(c) Find the exact probability that the smallest angle of $Q$ is more than $50°$
(5)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\dfrac{k}{10} + \dfrac{k}{20} + \dfrac{k}{30} + \dfrac{k}{40} + \dfrac{k}{50} = 1$ or $\dfrac{1}{600}(60k + 30k + 20k + 15k + 12k) = 1$ M1
So $k = \dfrac{600}{137}$ (*) A1cso
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for clear use of sum of probabilities = 1 (all terms seen). A1 cso (*) M1 scored and no incorrect working seen. Verify (Assume $k = \frac{600}{137}$) to score the final A1 they must have a final comment "$\therefore k = \frac{600}{137}$"
(b) (Cases are:) $D_1 = 30, D_2 = 50$ and $D_1 = 50, D_2 = 30$ and $D_1 = 40, D_2 = 40$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(D_1 + D_2 = 80) = \dfrac{k}{50} \times \dfrac{k}{30} \times 2 + \left(\dfrac{k}{40}\right)^2$ M1
$= 0.0375619\ldots$ awrt $\underline{0.0376}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for selecting at least 2 of the relevant cases (may be implied by their correct probs) e.g. allow 30, 50 and 50,30 i.e. $D_1$ and $D_2$ labels not required. 2nd M1 for using the model to obtain a correct expression for two different probabilities. May use letter $k$ or their value for $k$. Allow for $\frac{k}{50}\times\frac{k}{30}+\left(\frac{k}{40}\right)^2$ or $2\times\left(\frac{k}{50}\times\frac{k}{30}+\left(\frac{k}{40}\right)^2\right)$. A1 for awrt 0.0376 (exact fraction is $\frac{705}{18769}$)
(c) Angles are: $a$, $a+d$, $a+2d$, $a+3d$ M1
$S_4 = a + (a+d) + (a+2d) + (a+3d) = 360$ M1
$2a + 3d = 180$ (o.e.) A1
Smallest angle is $a > 50$ consider cases:
$d = 10$ so $a = 75$ or $d = 20$ so $a = 60$ [$d = 30$ gives $a = 45$ no good] M1
$\mathrm{P}(D = 10 \text{ or } 20) = \dfrac{3k}{20} = \dfrac{90}{137}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for recognising the 4 angles and finding expressions in terms of $d$ and their $a$. 2nd M1 for using property of quad with these 4 angles (equation can be un-simplified) Allow these two marks for use of a (possible) value of $d$ e.g. $a + a + 10 + a + 20 + a + 30 = 360$ (If at least 3 cases seen allow A1 for e.g. $4a = 300$) or allow M1M1 for a set of 4 angles with sum 360 and possible value of $d$ (3 cases for A1) e.g. (for $d = 20$) 60, 80, 100, 120
- 1st A1 for $2a + 3d = 180$ condition (o.e.) [Must be in the form $pa + qd = N$]. 3rd M1 for examining cases and getting $d = 10$ and $d = 20$ only. 2nd A1 for $\frac{90}{137}$ or exact equivalent. The correct answer and no obviously incorrect working will score 5/5. A final answer of awrt 0.657 (0.65693…) with no obviously incorrect working scores 4/5

questions.stem:
A health centre claims that the time a doctor spends with a patient can be modelled by a
normal distribution with a mean of 10 minutes and a standard deviation of 4 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Using this model, find the probability that the time spent with a randomly selected
patient is more than 15 minutes.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) {Let $X$ = time spent, $\mathrm{P}(X>15) =$} $0.105649\ldots$ awrt $\underline{0.106}$ B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for awrt 0.106 (from calculator) [Allow 10.6%]

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Some patients complain that the mean time the doctor spends with a patient is more than
10 minutes.

The receptionist takes a random sample of 20 patients and finds that the mean time the
doctor spends with a patient is 11.5 minutes.

(b) Stating your hypotheses clearly and using a 5% significance level, test whether or
not there is evidence to support the patients' complaint.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{H_0}: \mu = 10$ $\mathrm{H_1}: \mu > 10$ B1
$\bar{X} \sim \mathrm{N}\left(10, \left(\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{20}}\right)^2\right)$; $\mathrm{P}(\bar{X} > 11.5) = 0.046766\ldots$ [Condone $0.9532\ldots$] M1;A1
[This is significant ($<5\%$) so] there is evidence to support the complaint A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for both hypotheses correct in terms of $\mu$. M1 for selection of a correct model (sight or use of correct normal- may not have label $\bar{X}$) 1st A1 for use of this model to get probability allow 0.046~0.047 [Condone awrt 0.953]
- ALT OR test statistic $z$ = 1.677… (awrt 1.68) and cv of 1.64 (or better) or CR $\bar{X}$ > 11.47..
- 2nd A1 (dep on 1st A1 or at least $\mathrm{P}(\bar{X}>11.5)$ < 0.05 (o.e.)) for a correct conclusion in context -must mention complaint/claim or time/mins is > 10
- SC (M0 for $\bar{X}$ ~N(11.5, …)) for correct probability and conclusion (score M0A0A1 on epen)

parts.label: c(i)
parts.text:
The health centre also claims that the time a dentist spends with a patient during
a routine appointment, $T$ minutes, can be modelled by the normal distribution
where $T \sim \mathrm{N}(5, 3.5^2)$
(c) Using this model,
(i) find the probability that a routine appointment with the dentist takes less than 2
minutes
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) $[\mathrm{P}(T<2) =]$ $0.1956\ldots$ awrt $\underline{0.196}$ B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for awrt 0.196 (from calculator) [Allow 19.6%]

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.text:
(ii) find $\mathrm{P}(T<2 \mid T>0)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(ii) Require $\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(0<T<2)}{\mathrm{P}(T>0)} = \dfrac{0.119119\ldots}{0.923436\ldots}$; $= 0.1289955\ldots$ awrt $\underline{0.129}$ M1;A1;A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a correct probability ratio expression (may be implied by 1st A1 scored) 1st A1 for a correct ratio of probabilities (both correct or truncated to 2 dp) 2nd A1 for awrt 0.129

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.text:
(iii) hence explain why this normal distribution may not be a good model for $T$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(iii) The current model suggests non-negligible probability of $T$ values $< 0$ which
is impossible B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for a suitable explanation of why model is not suitable based on negative $T$ values Must say that a significant proportion of values < 0 (o.e.) e.g. P($T$ > 0) should be closer to 1 or Difference between P($T$ < 2| $T$ > 0) and P($T$ < 2) is too big (o.e.)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The dentist believes that she cannot complete a routine appointment in less than 2 minutes.

She suggests that the health centre should use a refined model only including values
of $T > 2$

(d) Find the median time for a routine appointment using this new model, giving your
answer correct to one decimal place.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) Require $t$ such that $\mathrm{P}(T>t \mid T>2) = 0.5$ or $\mathrm{P}(T<t \mid T>2) = 0.5$ M1
e.g. $\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(T>t)}{\mathrm{P}(T>2)} = 0.5$; so $\mathrm{P}(T>t) = 0.5 \times [1 - \text{(c)(i)}]$ or $\mathrm{P}(T>t) = 0.5 \times 0.8043\ldots$ M1;A1ft
[i.e. $\mathrm{P}(T>t) = 0.40\ldots$ implies] $\dfrac{t-5}{3.5} = 0.2533$ or $\mathrm{P}(T<t) = "0.5978\ldots"$ M1
$t = 5.886\ldots$ or from calculator $5.867\ldots$ so awrt $\underline{5.9}$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for a correct conditional probability statement to start the problem or 0.5$\times$P($T$ > 2) 2nd M1 for correct ratio of probability expressions [Must have P($T$ > $t$) or P(2 < $T$ < $t$)] 1st A1ft for a correct equation for P($T$ > $t$) (o.e.) ft their answer to part (c)[May be in a diagram] 3rd M1 for attempt to find $t$ (standardising and sight of 0.2533) or prepare to use calc (ft)
- Arriving at P($T$ < median) = 1 – 0.5$\times$"their 0.8043" will score 1st 4 marks. 2nd A1 for awrt 5.9. Sight of awrt 5.9 and at least one M mark scores 5/5 [Answer only send to review]
